DRAFT for owner approval (roadmap 4.6 step 3). It uses only archetypes,
code paths and format fields that exist today; nothing here asks for new

WHAT MAKES IT READ DIFFERENTLY FROM LEVEL 1, and it is one thing above all:
level 1 is six sectors of Heavy formations with a Wingman escort and never
more than ONE Light alive. Level 2 opens on a SWARM sector - subtype swarm,
Light ceiling 3, Heavy ceiling 0 - so the first thing the player meets is
three live Lights at once and no Heavy at all. That is the Light
multiplicity the project built for 4.6 and has never yet put in authored
data: level 1 has no Light-dominant wave anywhere.
The six sectors, and why each one is there:
1 SWARM   480 rows  interceptor + wingman, 3 Lights   the new opening
2 ELITE   640 rows  bomber + wingman ONLY             the bomber line
3 CAPITAL 542 rows  (the hull traversal is its clock) later than level 1
4 SWARM   768 rows  interceptor ONLY, 3 Lights, 16-frame floor
5 ELITE   800 rows  raider/bomber alternating
6 ELITE  1152 rows  all four archetypes; a Light wave inside an elite
THE CAPITAL SITS LATER THAN LEVEL 1'S, on the authored row 1,120 (480 +
640) instead of 272. The row is the clock, so the frame follows the
difficulty on its own - later on EASY, earlier on HARD (owner decision):
EASY 0.40 rows/frame -> ~frame 2,800   (56 s)
MEDIUM 0.45          -> ~frame 2,489   (50 s)
ESTIMATE from WORLD_SCROLL_RATE_{EASY,MEDIUM,HARD} = 8/9/10 over 20
(build/capital-hulls.inc); level 1's own 272 -> frame 606 MEDIUM is the
same arithmetic MEASURED, so the method is the level's, not a guess.
WAVE ROWS ARE 'NOT BEFORE' GATES, not a timetable. director_c_world_row_tick
returns early while STATE_WAVE_REMAINING is nonzero or light_wave_lock is up,
so an armed wave holds the cursor until it is spent and the next wave arms
the moment BOTH its row has passed and the previous wave has finished. Only
the SECTOR END can cut a wave list. Every sector below is therefore sized so
that all its waves are spent inside it on EASY, the slowest stream, at the
~30 rows per Heavy formation level 1 MEASURED (docs/level-authoring.md):
sector 2  18 formations -> 540 of 640 rows
sector 5  24 formations -> 720 of 800 rows
sector 6  30 formations + one 4-member Light wave -> ~948 of 1152 rows
The two swarm sectors carry the same headroom against an ESTIMATE of ~12
rows per Light admission on EASY, which is NOT measured yet - the Light
wave path has never run in authored data. Phase B measures it with
scripts/level-timeline.mjs and the sector lengths move if it is wrong.
ALTERNATION, level 1's owner decision 8, kept where it means anything:
sector 5 runs R,B,R,B and always spends all four, so it ENDS on bomber on
every difficulty and sector 6 opens on raider. Sector 2 is deliberately
three bomber waves in a row - that is the sector's identity, not an
accidental repeat, and no Heavy sector precedes or follows it directly.
WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT EXPRESS TODAY, named rather than faked:
* an enemy VARIANT (a recolour of an existing archetype) is wave
'appearance' 1-3, which the payload page carries and the runtime reads
from plan STEP 5. Every wave here is appearance 0, the archetype's own
art. There is no recolour in level 2 at step 3.
* 'look.stars' / 'look.nebula' per sector is step 5 as well, so every
sector leaves them at 0 rather than authoring a sky the build ignores.
* 'mirror' and 'afterCleared' compile into wave_flags but the Director
reads only WAVE_FLAG_HEAVY today, so neither is authored here.
* 'hazards.debris' is read as a nonzero TEST (HAZARD_DEBRIS_MASK), not as
a live count, so 1 and 2 behave alike today; the values below say what
the sector means and will bind when the count is read.
* hull length is plan STEP 4: level 2 flies today's 480-row hull.
Seed 77 (the plan's own §6 example) gives level 2 its own RNG stream:
director_c_init XORs it with the difficulty, so all three streams differ
from level 1's $6D.
